question.text: Two stones leave the ground at the same initial speed but at two different angles above the horizontal, and they both travel the same horizontal range. One of the stones is fired at π/3 and climbs to a peak height of 102 m. Find the peak height reached by the second stone, in metres.
conditions: both stones launched with the same initial speed
the two stones have equal horizontal ranges
first stone launched at π/3 to the horizontal

solution.approach: Equal range at the same speed means the two angles are complementary, so find the second angle and scale the given maximum height by the ratio of sine squares.

steps.text: For the same speed, two angles give the same range only if they are complementary, so the second angle is 90° − 60° = 30°.
Write the maximum height formula for both angles at the same speed u.
Divide the height at 30° by the height at 60°; the u² and 2g cancel.
Multiply the given height by this ratio to get the second height.

common_mistakes.text: Inverting the ratio, dividing the 60° height's sine-square term by the 30° height's sine-square term instead, gives 306 m, which is not among the printed options.
